mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points over the previous month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous 3 months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% year-over-year, it signals a tightening monetary policy coupled with slowing economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 over the previous month signals strong labor demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous 3 months signals a weakening supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 5% over the previous 3 months signals strong consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is below 2% annualized, it signals accommodative monetary policy coupled with low inflation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.
